rationale: Compound: ⲣⲉϥ- ('one who does') + ⲕⲗⲟⲩⲛⲟⲩ (etymology unclear; possibly Greek-derived from κλωνέω/κλόνος, or related to a wandering/turning verb). Context (alongside the elect 'laboring in the world... going around according to place to receive wages and beget money and wealth') supports an itinerant-worker / wage-earner sense. Confidence low; flagged for parallels.

Literal 'cutting-off forth' from ϣⲱⲱⲧ. In ascetic-soteriological register here designates the patiently-borne privation/lack the elect endures in secret among those without the hope of God. Distinct from the homonymous use 'separation forth' (cosmogonic). The fifth Mind-of-Light work is patience-of-this-privation.
Adverbial form on root ϩⲱⲡ 'hide' = 'in hiding, secretly.' Recurs lines 24 and 27 in the same passage characterizing the secret/hidden mode of the elect's privation. Standard Lyc adverbial.
Lycopolitan substantive likely reflex of ϩⲣⲟϣ-ϩⲏⲧ 'long-of-heart' or related ϩⲣⲏⲧⲉ 'manner of patience.' Standard Coptic virtue-noun for endurance. Listed as the fifth Mind-of-Light work.

proposed_english: they do not give (Lyc neg. habitual)
rationale: Lycopolitan negative habitual prefix ⲙⲁϩ- (= Sah ⲙⲉⲩ-) + ϯ 'give.' Confirmed by clausal context where the world-bound condition explains why no revelation reaches the elect during embodiment. Documents a Lyc dialectal feature.
